The University is an internationally renowned hub for art, design, digital media, research, innovation and creativity, and arts administration. The Faculty of Art invites applications for the following anticipated course offering in the Fall/Winter 2026\-27 academic year:

**FABR\-2002: Intro to FABR: Metal (0\.5 credit)**  

(Fall 2026 Semester: September 9, 2026 – December 23, 2026; Friday: 11:50AM \- 2:50PM; In\-Person)

**COURSE DESCRIPTION:** Students investigate a range of available metal products, techniques, and applications. Students also learn to work competently with basic tools and materials. Though an emphasis is placed upon skills development, students also explore the application of metal fabrication processes in contemporary art and design. Students are encouraged to link their metal fabrication projects to their studies in other areas.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:** Teaching and teaching\-related responsibilities may include but are not limited to: course outline development, studio preparation and delivery inclusive of lectures, critiques, grading, mid\-term evaluations and final evaluations/reviews; including responsibility for health \& safety and meeting academic and curricular requirements and deadlines.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* The successful applicant should have a terminal degree in art, design or relevant discipline and/or equivalent professional/practical experience
* Experience teaching at the post\-secondary level is considered an asset, equivalent relevant experience will be considered
* Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills
* Demonstrated leadership and experience promoting a respectful and inclusive work and learning environment for students, staff, and faculty
* Experience providing clear direction, mentorship and supervision to Teaching Assistants.

 **TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:** Sessional appointments are fixed\-term annual contracts. Sessional compensation includes a per\-course pay scale with salary level of $7,508\.00 (per 0\.5 credit course) plus 7% in lieu of benefits and vacation pay, per the provisions of the Employment Standards Act. These positions are subject to budgetary approval and satisfactory enrolment levels.

**Applications should include:**

* A letter of intent stating the candidate’s interests in the areas of teaching by identifying relevant courses above;
* A curriculum vitae;
* A statement of teaching philosophy that responds to the profile of the position;
* A **link or web address** to your digital portfolio of recent and current work/publications (if applicable)
* And the names and contact information of three references.

 *Please upload all five (5\) components (including the URL to work)* ***as one PDF****. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Please name your upload:* *FirstName\_LastName\-Job Code*


 Interested applicants are invited to submit their application in confidence, addressed to Faculty of Arts \& Science Appointments Committee, online**.**

**Please apply no later than August 12, 2026 11:59pm.**

***Applicants must be eligible to work in Canada for any employer (with a valid work or study permit, SIN and Canadian bank account).***

Job Description: **Job Title: Arts Administrator** 

Employee Position of 15 hours per week plus one weekend event per month, at $25 per hour.

**Posting Date: Wednesday July 22, 2026** 

**Closing Date: Wednesday July 29, 2026** 

**Reports to:** Board/Chair of Storytelling Toronto.

**Location:** Storytelling Toronto office, at the Wychwood Barns, 601 Christie Street, Studio 173\.

**Duration:** 12\-month contract with strong possibility for renewal. A 3\-month probationary period applies.

**Application:** to Laurie Malabar at hr@storytellingtoronto.org with your **First Name, Last Name and with Arts Administrator** in the subject line:

**1\)** Cover Letter

**2\)** Resume in PDF format

**3\)** Using https://sites.google.com/ design an imaginary storytelling event subpage using 3 storytellers from our directory, including their photos and bios. Send us a link to your design!

All applications will be reviewed, but only those shortlisted for an interview will be contacted.

**Here’s why this position is very important to Storytelling Toronto…** 

The Arts Administrator is the first point of contact with our members and with the public, responding to inquiries and promoting our activities through phone, website, newsletter and social media channels.

This position ensures the smooth running of the office, including purchasing supplies, organizing equipment and managing subscriptions. The Arts Administrator maintains files and email communications through Google Workspace.

This role is also essential for keeping our events running smoothly: setting up ticketing, organizing equipment and keeping performers and volunteers on schedule.

This role will require monthly production support for the Pillar event series and Festival events which happen on Saturdays. The Arts Administrator in concert with the Artistic Director, will ensure storytelling concerts, workshop, and the festival are delivered professionally and efficiently.

**Before you read further, you’ll need to have…** 

* Positive interpersonal skills communicating through computer, phone and in person
* Proven ability to independently and efficiently manage multiple tasks and timelines
* A Valid Driver’s License
* Previous production experience with live performances
* Confident decision\-making and collaboration skills when working with others
* Proficiency in layout, editing and graphic design (newsletters, survey forms and website content)
* Experience with Google Workspace, including administration
* Teleconferencing skills with Zoom and Google Meet
* Experience with social media, marketing and event promotion
* Event planning history including managing artist contracts, booking venues, renting equipment, ticketing and data collection
* Fluent oral and written English; proficiency in other languages, an asset
* Experience in practices of inclusion in all aspects of engagement

**And be able to apply your skills and experience in areas of:** 

1\) Member Engagement to

* Membership registration and renewal
* Actively rebuild and welcome interest in membership subscription and renewal
* Maintain and update the website
* Create communications about and provide administrative support for all ST activities
* Document and recognize contributions of all volunteers and donors

2\) Public Engagement to

* Provide first point of contact in a professional, timely manner on all inquiries
* Coordinate ticketing and audience services
* Publish ST activity news as submitted for social media, press and membership updates
* Ensure funders’ conditions are met consistently, such as use of logos, credits etc.
* Manage event registrations, cancellations and refunds
* Follow procedures on received cheques/cash collected for ST activities
* Manage charitable donations through PayPal, Wild Apricot and Canadahelps

3\) Board and Volunteer Engagement to

* Ensure new staff and volunteers receive an orientation package and follow up supports
* Track staff/artists/volunteers to complete HR training modules and send in signed contracts
* Prepare AGM documentation and send out required notification to membership
* Coordinate scheduling of online and in office use for all STT meetings
* Manage office landline and voice messaging and secure cloud storage

Pay: $25\.00 per hour

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Toronto, ON

Job Description: The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto\-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

**Purpose of Position** 

Reporting to the Manager, Registrar and Touring Exhibitions, the Registration Assistant will support the research, development, and implementation of a comprehensive Collections Emergency Salvage Plan to strengthen the Museum’s preparedness and response to collection\-related emergencies. This will involve identifying risks and preventive measures, developing response procedures, building internal and external response networks, and compiling research into a practical written plan for future use. In addition, the intern will assist with collections and registration activities, including condition reporting, art handling, packing and unpacking objects for transport, supporting temporary exhibitions, and completing collections documentation. The Registration Assistant will also support preventive conservation and work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams on ongoing exhibition projects.

**Program Stream:** Young Canada Works at Building Careers in Heritage (Graduates)

**Schedule:** Monday – Friday (32 hours per week)

**Contract Duration**: September 14, 2026 – March 31, 2027

**Hourly Rate:** $28/hr

**Positions Available**: 1

**Key Responsibilities**

· Conduct supervised research on current museum standards and best practices related to emergency preparedness and the recovery of collection objects following incidents such as floods, fires, power failures, or building system malfunctions.

· Review and summarize resources from recognized professional organizations, including AIC, AAM, ICOM, CCI, and regional museum associations.

· Compile research findings into reference materials to support the development or refinement of the Museum’s emergency response and collections recovery protocols.

· Consult with internal departments, including Collections, Conservation, Curatorial, Facilities, Security, and Visitor Services, to gather information on institutional needs, risks, and existing procedures.

· Participate in meetings and working groups focused on emergency preparedness, collections management, and storage reorganization, under staff supervision.

· Assist in integrating cross\-departmental feedback into practical, achievable workflows and guidelines for emergency situations and day\-to\-day collections care.

· Support outreach to peer institutions, local museums, conservation laboratories, emergency response services, freeze\-drying vendors, art handlers, and collections recovery specialists.

· Assist in developing and maintaining a contact list of external resources that could be mobilized in the event of an emergency.

· Document potential partnerships, service capabilities, and response timelines to support institutional emergency planning.

· Conduct visual condition assessments of artworks for temporary exhibitions, incoming and outgoing loans, and storage moves, under the guidance of Collections staff.

· Prepare clear, accurate written and photographic condition reports in accordance with institutional and professional standards.

· Identify and document existing damage, areas of vulnerability, and changes in condition, and communicate findings to Collections staff.

· Assist with the safe handling, packing, and unpacking of artworks for transport, storage moves, loans, and exhibitions.

· Prepare appropriate packing materials and housing solutions in consultation with Collections staff, ensuring compliance with museum standards for object safety and environmental protection.

· Assist in drafting, updating, and organizing policies and procedures related to collections storage, handling, movement, and loans.

· Support the implementation of policies and procedures by helping communicate guidelines to project staff and observing adherence during daily operations.

· Work collaboratively with Curatorial, Collections, and Exhibitions teams to support gallery rotations and temporary exhibitions.

· Assist with object preparation, documentation, transport coordination, and installation support.

· Participate in planning and coordinating storage and exhibition logistics to ensure the safe, timely, and organized movement of objects between storage and gallery spaces.

· Any other tasks assigned by the line manager.

**Qualifications \& Experience** 

· Bachelor’s degree in Art History, Museum Studies, Heritage Conservation, or a related field.

· Minimum of one year of experience drafting policies, procedures, or formal reports related to heritage or museum work.

· Experience in collections care, heritage preservation, or building conservation, including the ability to identify and assess risks to heritage collections and historic structures.

· High level of accuracy and attention to detail, with strong planning, organizational, and time\-management skills.

· Intermediate computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with digital documentation and record\-keeping; familiarity with collections management or conservation systems (e.g., The Museum System \[TMS]) is an asset.

· Knowledge of heritage preservation methods, including research, evaluation, handling, storage, and labelling of cultural artifacts or historic building materials, is an asset.

description: The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto\-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

**Purpose of Position** 

Reporting to the Manager, Registrar and Touring Exhibitions, the Registration Assistant will support the research, development, and implementation of a comprehensive Collections Emergency Salvage Plan to strengthen the Museum’s preparedness and response to collection\-related emergencies. This will involve identifying risks and preventive measures, developing response procedures, building internal and external response networks, and compiling research into a practical written plan for future use. In addition, the intern will assist with collections and registration activities, including condition reporting, art handling, packing and unpacking objects for transport, supporting temporary exhibitions, and completing collections documentation. The Registration Assistant will also support preventive conservation and work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams on ongoing exhibition projects.

**Program Stream:** Young Canada Works at Building Careers in Heritage (Graduates)

**Schedule:** Monday – Friday (32 hours per week)

**Contract Duration**: September 14, 2026 – March 31, 2027

**Hourly Rate:** $28/hr

**Positions Available**: 1

**Key Responsibilities**

· Conduct supervised research on current museum standards and best practices related to emergency preparedness and the recovery of collection objects following incidents such as floods, fires, power failures, or building system malfunctions.

· Review and summarize resources from recognized professional organizations, including AIC, AAM, ICOM, CCI, and regional museum associations.

· Compile research findings into reference materials to support the development or refinement of the Museum’s emergency response and collections recovery protocols.

· Consult with internal departments, including Collections, Conservation, Curatorial, Facilities, Security, and Visitor Services, to gather information on institutional needs, risks, and existing procedures.

· Participate in meetings and working groups focused on emergency preparedness, collections management, and storage reorganization, under staff supervision.

· Assist in integrating cross\-departmental feedback into practical, achievable workflows and guidelines for emergency situations and day\-to\-day collections care.

· Support outreach to peer institutions, local museums, conservation laboratories, emergency response services, freeze\-drying vendors, art handlers, and collections recovery specialists.

· Assist in developing and maintaining a contact list of external resources that could be mobilized in the event of an emergency.

· Document potential partnerships, service capabilities, and response timelines to support institutional emergency planning.

· Conduct visual condition assessments of artworks for temporary exhibitions, incoming and outgoing loans, and storage moves, under the guidance of Collections staff.

· Prepare clear, accurate written and photographic condition reports in accordance with institutional and professional standards.

· Identify and document existing damage, areas of vulnerability, and changes in condition, and communicate findings to Collections staff.

· Assist with the safe handling, packing, and unpacking of artworks for transport, storage moves, loans, and exhibitions.

· Prepare appropriate packing materials and housing solutions in consultation with Collections staff, ensuring compliance with museum standards for object safety and environmental protection.

· Assist in drafting, updating, and organizing policies and procedures related to collections storage, handling, movement, and loans.

· Support the implementation of policies and procedures by helping communicate guidelines to project staff and observing adherence during daily operations.

· Work collaboratively with Curatorial, Collections, and Exhibitions teams to support gallery rotations and temporary exhibitions.

· Assist with object preparation, documentation, transport coordination, and installation support.

· Participate in planning and coordinating storage and exhibition logistics to ensure the safe, timely, and organized movement of objects between storage and gallery spaces.

· Any other tasks assigned by the line manager.

**Qualifications \& Experience** 

· Bachelor’s degree in Art History, Museum Studies, Heritage Conservation, or a related field.

· Minimum of one year of experience drafting policies, procedures, or formal reports related to heritage or museum work.

· Experience in collections care, heritage preservation, or building conservation, including the ability to identify and assess risks to heritage collections and historic structures.

· High level of accuracy and attention to detail, with strong planning, organizational, and time\-management skills.

· Intermediate computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with digital documentation and record\-keeping; familiarity with collections management or conservation systems (e.g., The Museum System \[TMS]) is an asset.

· Knowledge of heritage preservation methods, including research, evaluation, handling, storage, and labelling of cultural artifacts or historic building materials, is an asset.

· Able to lift and carry up to 40 lb, stand for extended periods, and bend or lift overhead.

· Expressed interest in the mandate of the Museum.

The Museum encourages applications from youth in the community, including those who may face barriers to employment.

**Eligibility to Apply**

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

· Be between 16 and 30 years of age, inclusive, at the start of employment.

· Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person who has been granted refugee status in Canada.

· Be legally entitled to work in Canada and have a valid Social Insurance Number.

· Commit to the full duration of the contract period.

**Note:** 

· Non\-Canadian students holding temporary work visas or awaiting permanent resident status are not eligible.

· Priority will be given to graduates who have not previously participated in Young Canada Works internship programs and who are unemployed or underemployed.

**To Apply**

Please send your resume to **akm.hr@akdn.org** by **July 31, 2026\.**

The Museum thanks all those who apply; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that the Museum is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fair and accessible employment practices. Upon request, suitable accommodations are available under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act for applicants invited to an interview. The Museum encourages applications by individuals identifying as Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ\+ persons, members of visible minorities and/or anyone belonging to equity\-deserving groups.

Pay: $28\.00 per hour

Benefits:

* On\-site parking

MNR facilitates and enables dozens of investigators from approximately 25 Universities to conduct foundational and translational research by providing operational, analytical, technical, regulatory and project management staffing for faculty\-led research initiatives, and training and support services for researchers who wish to work independently.

Framed by critical discourse on documentary media, as well as historical and contemporary examples, this course explores animation as a potent tool for elaborating non-fiction projects. Job Description: **Rumble** is *the* Freedom\-First technology platform. We proudly offer a video platform, cloud services, advertising solutions, and a non\-custodial cryptocurrency wallet.


Rumble is seeking a Brand Designer to create bold, high\-impact visual work across our brand, marketing, creator, and business initiatives. This role is ideal for a designer who can translate ideas into clear, compelling creative across a wide range of formats, from landing pages and social assets to presentations, event materials, and campaign collateral. You'll help shape how Rumble shows up to creators, users, advertisers, and partners across a fast\-growing video platform built around independent voices and audience connection.



In this role, you'll bring Rumble's suite of brands to life through thoughtful, high\-quality design that is both consistent and adaptable. You should be comfortable owning work from concept to final delivery, creating reusable assets, and developing visuals that support marketing, storytelling, and business growth. Success in this role requires strong creative instincts, attention to detail, and the ability to move quickly under tight deadlines without losing sight of brand standards or strategic intent.



You'll work closely with cross\-functional partners while also collaborating with external creatives, including artists, photographers, and agencies, when needed. This role does not have a dedicated project manager, so the right candidate must be highly self\-directed, organized, and accountable for driving their own work forward. The ideal candidate is energized by a fast\-moving environment where priorities can shift and where strong design plays an important role in how the company communicates with multiple audiences.


**Responsibilities**
--------------------



Lead brand and marketing design work across a broad mix of channels, campaigns, and business needs. Create high\-quality illustrations, graphics, and other visual assets from concept through final delivery. Build and maintain reusable creative assets such as landing pages, display ads, social media content, marketing decks, presentations, event materials, and other branded collateral. Manage multiple projects independently, prioritize effectively, and deliver high\-quality work under tight timelines without day\-to\-day project management support. Partner with cross\-functional teams to develop visuals that connect with creators, Rumble users, advertisers, and business audiences. Help enforce consistency across the organization by applying and championing brand guidelines. Coordinate with external creative partners when additional support or specialized assets are needed. Contribute to other creative and brand initiatives as priorities evolve.


**Qualifications**
------------------


* 3\+ years of professional design experience, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong brand and marketing work across multiple channels and asset types.
* 3\+ years of experience designing email creative, ideally in Figma or a comparable design environment.
* Experience producing digital, presentation, and large\-format creative assets.
* Strong understanding of how to connect brand or marketing strategy to effective visual design.
* Proficiency in Figma and strong command of design fundamentals including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition.
* Comfort working in a fast\-paced environment with changing priorities, tight deadlines, and multiple concurrent projects.
* Highly self\-directed, proactive, and organized, with the ability to manage work independently and own outcomes in an environment without dedicated project management support.
* General understanding of performance and growth marketing, and how creative work supports campaign outcomes.
* Strong collaboration and communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with cross\-functional teams and outside creative partners.
* Comfort working in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office products, especially for presentation, document, and collaborative asset development.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------


* Experience designing for technology, media, creator\-focused, or advertising\-related businesses.
* Experience creating social assets for platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.
* Agency background or experience supporting multiple brands, campaigns, or audiences in parallel.
* Bachelor's degree in Design, Creative, Visual Communication, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience creating work that supports creator programs, audience growth, advertising, or brand partnerships.


**Annual Compensation Range:**



$100,000 \- $120,000 USD base \+ benefits \+ equity (If based in the United States)



Note: The salary range listed for this position is a good faith estimate based on experience, qualifications, and internal compensation structure. The actual salary offered varies depending on the candidate's skill level and experience. This posting refers to an active vacancy within the organization.

**Why Our Team Loves Working Here:**


* We are making a significant financial impact for our video creator community; we're proud of their success stories
* We enjoy challenging the status quo and going head\-to\-head against Big Tech
* We aren't afraid to try new things; we act fast and want to win
* We pay competitive salaries and provide great benefits


**EEO Statement:**  

Rumble is an equal opportunity employer. We promote an equal playing field where everyone has the same opportunities regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law. Rumble is an active participant in the e\-verify program.


**Physical demands of the position:**  

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods of time while using a computer and/or keyboard. The employee is required to communicate verbally and hear. The employee may be required to walk, reach with hands and arms, balance, and stoop or kneel. The employee may occasionally be required to lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. * Create designs that communicate a clear vision aligning with client expectations
* Create a variety of layout options based on client briefs/guidelines
* Offer new and innovative ideas to the client

* Design original artwork, create mock\-ups, \& manipulate images in Photoshop
* Work closely with the Sales Representatives and Project Coordinators on projects

* Source images from stock photo sites as needed
* Preflight files
* Can be flexible with work hours during busy work periods, may involve working some evenings

**Skills, Experience and Requirements**

* A post\-secondary degree or diploma in Graphic Design or closely related field
* 3\-5 years of experience in the Graphic Design field
* A strong portfolio that showcases a diversity of print pieces that are sleek, modern, and clean in style
* Proficient with Adobe Creative Suite on a MAC platform
* CAD/3D Rendering is an asset

**Key Competencies**

* Creative mind
* Works well in collaborative and independent work environment
* Strong design and layout skills
* Proactive and organized
* Expert time\-management skills, ability to work with tight deadlines and urgency
* An understanding of color modes, resolution and file formats for large and small format print

ICON is a full\-service organization with a 120,000 square foot state\-of\-the\-art production facility based in Markham, Ontario. Job Description: **Job Title: Arts Administrator** 

Employee Position of 15 hours per week plus one weekend event per month, at $25 per hour.

**Posting Date: Wednesday July 22, 2026** 

**Closing Date: Wednesday July 29, 2026** 

**Reports to:** Board/Chair of Storytelling Toronto.

**Location:** Storytelling Toronto office, at the Wychwood Barns, 601 Christie Street, Studio 173\.

**Duration:** 12\-month contract with strong possibility for renewal. A 3\-month probationary period applies.

**Application:** to Laurie Malabar at hr@storytellingtoronto.org with your **First Name, Last Name and with Arts Administrator** in the subject line:

**1\)** Cover Letter

**2\)** Resume in PDF format

**3\)** Using https://sites.google.com/ design an imaginary storytelling event subpage using 3 storytellers from our directory, including their photos and bios. Send us a link to your design!

All applications will be reviewed, but only those shortlisted for an interview will be contacted.

**Here’s why this position is very important to Storytelling Toronto…** 

The Arts Administrator is the first point of contact with our members and with the public, responding to inquiries and promoting our activities through phone, website, newsletter and social media channels.

This position ensures the smooth running of the office, including purchasing supplies, organizing equipment and managing subscriptions. The Arts Administrator maintains files and email communications through Google Workspace.

This role is also essential for keeping our events running smoothly: setting up ticketing, organizing equipment and keeping performers and volunteers on schedule.

This role will require monthly production support for the Pillar event series and Festival events which happen on Saturdays. The Arts Administrator in concert with the Artistic Director, will ensure storytelling concerts, workshop, and the festival are delivered professionally and efficiently.

**Before you read further, you’ll need to have…** 

* Positive interpersonal skills communicating through computer, phone and in person
* Proven ability to independently and efficiently manage multiple tasks and timelines
* A Valid Driver’s License
* Previous production experience with live performances
* Confident decision\-making and collaboration skills when working with others
* Proficiency in layout, editing and graphic design (newsletters, survey forms and website content)
* Experience with Google Workspace, including administration
* Teleconferencing skills with Zoom and Google Meet
* Experience with social media, marketing and event promotion
* Event planning history including managing artist contracts, booking venues, renting equipment, ticketing and data collection
* Fluent oral and written English; proficiency in other languages, an asset
* Experience in practices of inclusion in all aspects of engagement

**And be able to apply your skills and experience in areas of:** 

1\) Member Engagement to

* Membership registration and renewal
* Actively rebuild and welcome interest in membership subscription and renewal
* Maintain and update the website
* Create communications about and provide administrative support for all ST activities
* Document and recognize contributions of all volunteers and donors

2\) Public Engagement to

* Provide first point of contact in a professional, timely manner on all inquiries
* Coordinate ticketing and audience services
* Publish ST activity news as submitted for social media, press and membership updates
* Ensure funders’ conditions are met consistently, such as use of logos, credits etc.
* Manage event registrations, cancellations and refunds
* Follow procedures on received cheques/cash collected for ST activities
* Manage charitable donations through PayPal, Wild Apricot and Canadahelps

3\) Board and Volunteer Engagement to

* Ensure new staff and volunteers receive an orientation package and follow up supports
* Track staff/artists/volunteers to complete HR training modules and send in signed contracts
* Prepare AGM documentation and send out required notification to membership
* Coordinate scheduling of online and in office use for all STT meetings
* Manage office landline and voice messaging and secure cloud storage

Pay: $25\.00 per hour

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Toronto, ON

Job Description: The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto\-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

**Purpose of Position** 

Reporting to the Manager, Registrar and Touring Exhibitions, the Registration Assistant will support the research, development, and implementation of a comprehensive Collections Emergency Salvage Plan to strengthen the Museum’s preparedness and response to collection\-related emergencies. This will involve identifying risks and preventive measures, developing response procedures, building internal and external response networks, and compiling research into a practical written plan for future use. In addition, the intern will assist with collections and registration activities, including condition reporting, art handling, packing and unpacking objects for transport, supporting temporary exhibitions, and completing collections documentation. The Registration Assistant will also support preventive conservation and work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams on ongoing exhibition projects.

**Program Stream:** Young Canada Works at Building Careers in Heritage (Graduates)

**Schedule:** Monday – Friday (32 hours per week)

**Contract Duration**: September 14, 2026 – March 31, 2027

**Hourly Rate:** $28/hr

**Positions Available**: 1

**Key Responsibilities**

· Conduct supervised research on current museum standards and best practices related to emergency preparedness and the recovery of collection objects following incidents such as floods, fires, power failures, or building system malfunctions.

· Review and summarize resources from recognized professional organizations, including AIC, AAM, ICOM, CCI, and regional museum associations.

· Compile research findings into reference materials to support the development or refinement of the Museum’s emergency response and collections recovery protocols.

· Consult with internal departments, including Collections, Conservation, Curatorial, Facilities, Security, and Visitor Services, to gather information on institutional needs, risks, and existing procedures.

· Participate in meetings and working groups focused on emergency preparedness, collections management, and storage reorganization, under staff supervision.

· Assist in integrating cross\-departmental feedback into practical, achievable workflows and guidelines for emergency situations and day\-to\-day collections care.

· Support outreach to peer institutions, local museums, conservation laboratories, emergency response services, freeze\-drying vendors, art handlers, and collections recovery specialists.

· Assist in developing and maintaining a contact list of external resources that could be mobilized in the event of an emergency.

· Document potential partnerships, service capabilities, and response timelines to support institutional emergency planning.

· Conduct visual condition assessments of artworks for temporary exhibitions, incoming and outgoing loans, and storage moves, under the guidance of Collections staff.

· Prepare clear, accurate written and photographic condition reports in accordance with institutional and professional standards.

· Identify and document existing damage, areas of vulnerability, and changes in condition, and communicate findings to Collections staff.

· Assist with the safe handling, packing, and unpacking of artworks for transport, storage moves, loans, and exhibitions.

· Prepare appropriate packing materials and housing solutions in consultation with Collections staff, ensuring compliance with museum standards for object safety and environmental protection.

· Assist in drafting, updating, and organizing policies and procedures related to collections storage, handling, movement, and loans.

· Support the implementation of policies and procedures by helping communicate guidelines to project staff and observing adherence during daily operations.

· Work collaboratively with Curatorial, Collections, and Exhibitions teams to support gallery rotations and temporary exhibitions.

· Assist with object preparation, documentation, transport coordination, and installation support.

· Participate in planning and coordinating storage and exhibition logistics to ensure the safe, timely, and organized movement of objects between storage and gallery spaces.

· Any other tasks assigned by the line manager.

**Qualifications \& Experience** 

· Bachelor’s degree in Art History, Museum Studies, Heritage Conservation, or a related field.

· Minimum of one year of experience drafting policies, procedures, or formal reports related to heritage or museum work.

· Experience in collections care, heritage preservation, or building conservation, including the ability to identify and assess risks to heritage collections and historic structures.

· High level of accuracy and attention to detail, with strong planning, organizational, and time\-management skills.

· Intermediate computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with digital documentation and record\-keeping; familiarity with collections management or conservation systems (e.g., The Museum System \[TMS]) is an asset.

· Knowledge of heritage preservation methods, including research, evaluation, handling, storage, and labelling of cultural artifacts or historic building materials, is an asset.

· Able to lift and carry up to 40 lb, stand for extended periods, and bend or lift overhead.

· Expressed interest in the mandate of the Museum.

The Museum encourages applications from youth in the community, including those who may face barriers to employment.

**Eligibility to Apply**

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

· Be between 16 and 30 years of age, inclusive, at the start of employment.

· Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person who has been granted refugee status in Canada.

· Be legally entitled to work in Canada and have a valid Social Insurance Number.

· Commit to the full duration of the contract period.

**Note:** 

· Non\-Canadian students holding temporary work visas or awaiting permanent resident status are not eligible.

· Priority will be given to graduates who have not previously participated in Young Canada Works internship programs and who are unemployed or underemployed.

**To Apply**

Please send your resume to **akm.hr@akdn.org** by **July 31, 2026\.**

The Museum thanks all those who apply; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that the Museum is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fair and accessible employment practices. Upon request, suitable accommodations are available under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act for applicants invited to an interview. The Museum encourages applications by individuals identifying as Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ\+ persons, members of visible minorities and/or anyone belonging to equity\-deserving groups.

Pay: $28\.00 per hour

Benefits:

* On\-site parking

Work Location: In person

Job Description  

  

  

**Department Description:**  

The McMaster Nuclear Reactor (MNR) is a unique combination of commercial operations, research, and teaching facilities. The facility consists of the McMaster Nuclear Reactor and NRB support facilities including Centre for Advanced Nuclear Systems, Small Angle Neutron Scattering, Accelerator, McMaster University Cyclotron Facility, High Level Laboratory Facility, McMaster Positron facility and 9 other cost centres within MNR.
  

MNR facilitates and enables dozens of investigators from approximately 25 Universities to conduct foundational and translational research by providing operational, analytical, technical, regulatory and project management staffing for faculty\-led research initiatives, and training and support services for researchers who wish to work independently.
  

Nuclear Operations \& Facilities has recently developed a hot lab in MUMC and will be producing product, packaging and shipping patient doses of a new radioisotope in support of the North American trials of the product (Ho 166 liver cancer therapeutic)  

  



**Job Summary:**  

Provide support to research projects in a laboratory environment. Work is standardized and performed, under general direction and guidance.  

  



**Accountabilities:**  

1\. Assist investigators in obtaining scientific data by performing standardized laboratory experiments under general supervision and guidance.
  

2\. Observe, detail, record, and maintain accurate records of experimental protocols, conditions, and results.
  

3\. Apply established research methodology to ensure all research material is handled in accordance with established protocols, policies and procedures.
  

4\. Conduct literature searches to support the research project.
  

5\. Seek guidance and direction from Research Staff or Manager.
  

6\. Electrical and mechanical component diagnostic and repair
  

7\. Assist with daily/planned maintenance for various facility equipment


**Qualifications:**  

Education: Completed or currently enrolled in a relevant post\-secondary program.
  

Experience: Prior exposure to a laboratory environment.  

  



**Assets:**  

* Experience with Pneumatic automation system
* Experience with PLC programming
**Nuclear Operations Security Provisions**  

Security clearances and background checks are necessary due to the sensitive nature of the nuclear facility’s operations and regulatory licensing (Nuclear Safety Control Act) requirements. As a condition of employment for this Appointment, you must successfully complete the appropriate and necessary security screenings / clearances (documentation will follow in a separate email). You will be advised in writing by the University whether this condition has been met upon the University's receipt of the results. If you are unsuccessful in these processes, you will not be able to meet the job requirements and therefore any offer of employment will be rescinded or will result in your employment with the University will be terminated.  

  



**Being a Nuclear Energy Worker**  

You will be declared a Nuclear Energy Worker. Given the nature of the work environment where you will be performing your duties, which includes entering and working in radiological hazardous environments, the University requires the use of protective equipment such as respirators, protective clothing, and gloves, as necessary to enter these areas. The University is committed to fostering a safe and healthy work environment

The Faculty of ​Art​ invites applications for the following anticipated course offering in the Fall/Winter 2026-27 academic year:
EXAN-3009: Animated Documentary (​0.5​ credit)
(Fall 2026 Semester: September 9, 2026 – December 23, 2026; Thursday: 3:10PM - 6:10PM; Blended Delivery)
COURSE DESCRIPTION:
Framed by critical discourse on documentary media, as well as historical and contemporary examples, this course explores animation as a potent tool for elaborating non-fiction projects. Drawing on documentation, students will learn to use animation to deliver engaged commentary on issues of social and political relevance or translate personal narratives through animated media. Students will also explore the shifting notions of truth and ethical dilemmas inherent to documentary film-making and essayist videos. Through a blend of theory and practice, this course will deepen students' understanding of the unique power of animation in conveying complex non-fiction narratives.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching and teaching-related responsibilities may include but are not limited to: course outline development, studio preparation and delivery inclusive of lectures, critiques, grading, mid-term evaluations and final evaluations/reviews; including responsibility for health & safety and meeting academic and curricular requirements and deadlines.

The successful applicant should have a terminal degree in art, design or relevant discipline and/or equivalent professional/practical experience
Experience teaching at the post-secondary level is considered an asset, equivalent relevant experience will be considered
Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills
Demonstrated leadership and experience promoting a respectful and inclusive work and learning environment for students, staff, and faculty
Experience providing clear direction, mentorship and supervision to Teaching Assistants.

Job Description: **Rumble** is *the* Freedom\-First technology platform. We proudly offer a video platform, cloud services, advertising solutions, and a non\-custodial cryptocurrency wallet.


Rumble is seeking a Brand Designer to create bold, high\-impact visual work across our brand, marketing, creator, and business initiatives. This role is ideal for a designer who can translate ideas into clear, compelling creative across a wide range of formats, from landing pages and social assets to presentations, event materials, and campaign collateral. You'll help shape how Rumble shows up to creators, users, advertisers, and partners across a fast\-growing video platform built around independent voices and audience connection.



In this role, you'll bring Rumble's suite of brands to life through thoughtful, high\-quality design that is both consistent and adaptable. You should be comfortable owning work from concept to final delivery, creating reusable assets, and developing visuals that support marketing, storytelling, and business growth. Success in this role requires strong creative instincts, attention to detail, and the ability to move quickly under tight deadlines without losing sight of brand standards or strategic intent.



You'll work closely with cross\-functional partners while also collaborating with external creatives, including artists, photographers, and agencies, when needed. This role does not have a dedicated project manager, so the right candidate must be highly self\-directed, organized, and accountable for driving their own work forward. The ideal candidate is energized by a fast\-moving environment where priorities can shift and where strong design plays an important role in how the company communicates with multiple audiences.


**Responsibilities**
--------------------



Lead brand and marketing design work across a broad mix of channels, campaigns, and business needs. Create high\-quality illustrations, graphics, and other visual assets from concept through final delivery. Build and maintain reusable creative assets such as landing pages, display ads, social media content, marketing decks, presentations, event materials, and other branded collateral. Manage multiple projects independently, prioritize effectively, and deliver high\-quality work under tight timelines without day\-to\-day project management support. Partner with cross\-functional teams to develop visuals that connect with creators, Rumble users, advertisers, and business audiences. Help enforce consistency across the organization by applying and championing brand guidelines. Coordinate with external creative partners when additional support or specialized assets are needed. Contribute to other creative and brand initiatives as priorities evolve.


**Qualifications**
------------------


* 3\+ years of professional design experience, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong brand and marketing work across multiple channels and asset types.
* 3\+ years of experience designing email creative, ideally in Figma or a comparable design environment.
* Experience producing digital, presentation, and large\-format creative assets.
* Strong understanding of how to connect brand or marketing strategy to effective visual design.
* Proficiency in Figma and strong command of design fundamentals including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition.
* Comfort working in a fast\-paced environment with changing priorities, tight deadlines, and multiple concurrent projects.
* Highly self\-directed, proactive, and organized, with the ability to manage work independently and own outcomes in an environment without dedicated project management support.
* General understanding of performance and growth marketing, and how creative work supports campaign outcomes.
* Strong collaboration and communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with cross\-functional teams and outside creative partners.
* Comfort working in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office products, especially for presentation, document, and collaborative asset development.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------


* Experience designing for technology, media, creator\-focused, or advertising\-related businesses.
* Experience creating social assets for platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.
* Agency background or experience supporting multiple brands, campaigns, or audiences in parallel.
* Bachelor's degree in Design, Creative, Visual Communication, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience creating work that supports creator programs, audience growth, advertising, or brand partnerships.


**Annual Compensation Range:**



$100,000 \- $120,000 USD base \+ benefits \+ equity (If based in the United States)



Note: The salary range listed for this position is a good faith estimate based on experience, qualifications, and internal compensation structure. The actual salary offered varies depending on the candidate's skill level and experience. This posting refers to an active vacancy within the organization.

**Why Our Team Loves Working Here:**


* We are making a significant financial impact for our video creator community; we're proud of their success stories
* We enjoy challenging the status quo and going head\-to\-head against Big Tech
* We aren't afraid to try new things; we act fast and want to win
* We pay competitive salaries and provide great benefits


**EEO Statement:**  

Rumble is an equal opportunity employer. We promote an equal playing field where everyone has the same opportunities regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law. Rumble is an active participant in the e\-verify program.


**Physical demands of the position:**  

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods of time while using a computer and/or keyboard. The employee is required to communicate verbally and hear. The employee may be required to walk, reach with hands and arms, balance, and stoop or kneel. The employee may occasionally be required to lift and/or move up to 15 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include clarity of vision at approximately 20 inches or less (i.e., working with small objects or reading small print), including the use of computers.

Job Description: **Job Title: Arts Administrator** 

Employee Position of 15 hours per week plus one weekend event per month, at $25 per hour.

**Posting Date: Wednesday July 22, 2026** 

**Closing Date: Wednesday July 29, 2026** 

**Reports to:** Board/Chair of Storytelling Toronto.

**Location:** Storytelling Toronto office, at the Wychwood Barns, 601 Christie Street, Studio 173\.

**Duration:** 12\-month contract with strong possibility for renewal. A 3\-month probationary period applies.

**Application:** to Laurie Malabar at hr@storytellingtoronto.org with your **First Name, Last Name and with Arts Administrator** in the subject line:

**1\)** Cover Letter

**2\)** Resume in PDF format

**3\)** Using https://sites.google.com/ design an imaginary storytelling event subpage using 3 storytellers from our directory, including their photos and bios. Send us a link to your design!

All applications will be reviewed, but only those shortlisted for an interview will be contacted.

**Here’s why this position is very important to Storytelling Toronto…** 

The Arts Administrator is the first point of contact with our members and with the public, responding to inquiries and promoting our activities through phone, website, newsletter and social media channels.

This position ensures the smooth running of the office, including purchasing supplies, organizing equipment and managing subscriptions. The Arts Administrator maintains files and email communications through Google Workspace.

This role is also essential for keeping our events running smoothly: setting up ticketing, organizing equipment and keeping performers and volunteers on schedule.

This role will require monthly production support for the Pillar event series and Festival events which happen on Saturdays. The Arts Administrator in concert with the Artistic Director, will ensure storytelling concerts, workshop, and the festival are delivered professionally and efficiently.

**Before you read further, you’ll need to have…** 

* Positive interpersonal skills communicating through computer, phone and in person
* Proven ability to independently and efficiently manage multiple tasks and timelines
* A Valid Driver’s License
* Previous production experience with live performances
* Confident decision\-making and collaboration skills when working with others
* Proficiency in layout, editing and graphic design (newsletters, survey forms and website content)
* Experience with Google Workspace, including administration
* Teleconferencing skills with Zoom and Google Meet
* Experience with social media, marketing and event promotion
* Event planning history including managing artist contracts, booking venues, renting equipment, ticketing and data collection
* Fluent oral and written English; proficiency in other languages, an asset
* Experience in practices of inclusion in all aspects of engagement

**And be able to apply your skills and experience in areas of:** 

1\) Member Engagement to

* Membership registration and renewal
* Actively rebuild and welcome interest in membership subscription and renewal
* Maintain and update the website
* Create communications about and provide administrative support for all ST activities
* Document and recognize contributions of all volunteers and donors

2\) Public Engagement to

* Provide first point of contact in a professional, timely manner on all inquiries
* Coordinate ticketing and audience services
* Publish ST activity news as submitted for social media, press and membership updates
* Ensure funders’ conditions are met consistently, such as use of logos, credits etc.
* Manage event registrations, cancellations and refunds
* Follow procedures on received cheques/cash collected for ST activities
* Manage charitable donations through PayPal, Wild Apricot and Canadahelps

3\) Board and Volunteer Engagement to

* Ensure new staff and volunteers receive an orientation package and follow up supports
* Track staff/artists/volunteers to complete HR training modules and send in signed contracts
* Prepare AGM documentation and send out required notification to membership
* Coordinate scheduling of online and in office use for all STT meetings
* Manage office landline and voice messaging and secure cloud storage

Pay: $25\.00 per hour

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Toronto, ON

Job Description: The Aga Khan Museum connects cultures and communities through the arts. The Museum’s mission is to spark wonder, curiosity, and understanding of Muslim cultures and their connection with other cultures through the arts.

The Toronto\-based Museum promotes pluralism through art, storytelling, and enlightened encounters across cultures. Using traditional and contemporary art as well as performing arts as a force for positive change, the Museum’s vision is to impact lives and contribute to more inclusive and peaceful societies. The Museum acts as a global learning hub, playing a unique and pivotal role in building connections between people and communities locally, nationally, and internationally.

**Purpose of Position** 

Reporting to the Manager, Registrar and Touring Exhibitions, the Registration Assistant will support the research, development, and implementation of a comprehensive Collections Emergency Salvage Plan to strengthen the Museum’s preparedness and response to collection\-related emergencies. This will involve identifying risks and preventive measures, developing response procedures, building internal and external response networks, and compiling research into a practical written plan for future use. In addition, the intern will assist with collections and registration activities, including condition reporting, art handling, packing and unpacking objects for transport, supporting temporary exhibitions, and completing collections documentation. The Registration Assistant will also support preventive conservation and work closely with the Curatorial and Exhibitions teams on ongoing exhibition projects.

**Program Stream:** Young Canada Works at Building Careers in Heritage (Graduates)

**Schedule:** Monday – Friday (32 hours per week)

**Contract Duration**: September 14, 2026 – March 31, 2027

**Hourly Rate:** $28/hr

**Positions Available**: 1

**Key Responsibilities**

· Conduct supervised research on current museum standards and best practices related to emergency preparedness and the recovery of collection objects following incidents such as floods, fires, power failures, or building system malfunctions.

· Review and summarize resources from recognized professional organizations, including AIC, AAM, ICOM, CCI, and regional museum associations.

· Compile research findings into reference materials to support the development or refinement of the Museum’s emergency response and collections recovery protocols.

· Consult with internal departments, including Collections, Conservation, Curatorial, Facilities, Security, and Visitor Services, to gather information on institutional needs, risks, and existing procedures.

· Participate in meetings and working groups focused on emergency preparedness, collections management, and storage reorganization, under staff supervision.

· Assist in integrating cross\-departmental feedback into practical, achievable workflows and guidelines for emergency situations and day\-to\-day collections care.

· Support outreach to peer institutions, local museums, conservation laboratories, emergency response services, freeze\-drying vendors, art handlers, and collections recovery specialists.

· Assist in developing and maintaining a contact list of external resources that could be mobilized in the event of an emergency.

· Document potential partnerships, service capabilities, and response timelines to support institutional emergency planning.

· Conduct visual condition assessments of artworks for temporary exhibitions, incoming and outgoing loans, and storage moves, under the guidance of Collections staff.

· Prepare clear, accurate written and photographic condition reports in accordance with institutional and professional standards.

· Identify and document existing damage, areas of vulnerability, and changes in condition, and communicate findings to Collections staff.

· Assist with the safe handling, packing, and unpacking of artworks for transport, storage moves, loans, and exhibitions.

· Prepare appropriate packing materials and housing solutions in consultation with Collections staff, ensuring compliance with museum standards for object safety and environmental protection.

· Assist in drafting, updating, and organizing policies and procedures related to collections storage, handling, movement, and loans.

· Support the implementation of policies and procedures by helping communicate guidelines to project staff and observing adherence during daily operations.

· Work collaboratively with Curatorial, Collections, and Exhibitions teams to support gallery rotations and temporary exhibitions.

· Assist with object preparation, documentation, transport coordination, and installation support.

· Participate in planning and coordinating storage and exhibition logistics to ensure the safe, timely, and organized movement of objects between storage and gallery spaces.

· Any other tasks assigned by the line manager.

**Qualifications \& Experience** 

· Bachelor’s degree in Art History, Museum Studies, Heritage Conservation, or a related field.

· Minimum of one year of experience drafting policies, procedures, or formal reports related to heritage or museum work.

· Experience in collections care, heritage preservation, or building conservation, including the ability to identify and assess risks to heritage collections and historic structures.

· High level of accuracy and attention to detail, with strong planning, organizational, and time\-management skills.

· Intermediate computer skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with digital documentation and record\-keeping; familiarity with collections management or conservation systems (e.g., The Museum System \[TMS]) is an asset.

· Knowledge of heritage preservation methods, including research, evaluation, handling, storage, and labelling of cultural artifacts or historic building materials, is an asset.

· Able to lift and carry up to 40 lb, stand for extended periods, and bend or lift overhead.

· Expressed interest in the mandate of the Museum.

The Museum encourages applications from youth in the community, including those who may face barriers to employment.

**Eligibility to Apply**

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements:

· Be between 16 and 30 years of age, inclusive, at the start of employment.

· Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person who has been granted refugee status in Canada.

· Be legally entitled to work in Canada and have a valid Social Insurance Number.

· Commit to the full duration of the contract period.

**Note:** 

· Non\-Canadian students holding temporary work visas or awaiting permanent resident status are not eligible.

· Priority will be given to graduates who have not previously participated in Young Canada Works internship programs and who are unemployed or underemployed.

**To Apply**

Please send your resume to **akm.hr@akdn.org** by **July 31, 2026\.**

The Museum thanks all those who apply; however, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Please note that the Museum is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fair and accessible employment practices. Upon request, suitable accommodations are available under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act for applicants invited to an interview. The Museum encourages applications by individuals identifying as Indigenous peoples, racialized persons/persons of colour, persons with disabilities, women, 2SLGBTQ\+ persons, members of visible minorities and/or anyone belonging to equity\-deserving groups.

Pay: $28\.00 per hour

Benefits:

* On\-site parking

Work Location: In person

Job Description  

  

  

**Department Description:**  

The McMaster Nuclear Reactor (MNR) is a unique combination of commercial operations, research, and teaching facilities. The facility consists of the McMaster Nuclear Reactor and NRB support facilities including Centre for Advanced Nuclear Systems, Small Angle Neutron Scattering, Accelerator, McMaster University Cyclotron Facility, High Level Laboratory Facility, McMaster Positron facility and 9 other cost centres within MNR.
  

MNR facilitates and enables dozens of investigators from approximately 25 Universities to conduct foundational and translational research by providing operational, analytical, technical, regulatory and project management staffing for faculty\-led research initiatives, and training and support services for researchers who wish to work independently.
  

Nuclear Operations \& Facilities has recently developed a hot lab in MUMC and will be producing product, packaging and shipping patient doses of a new radioisotope in support of the North American trials of the product (Ho 166 liver cancer therapeutic)  

  



**Job Summary:**  

Provide support to research projects in a laboratory environment. Work is standardized and performed, under general direction and guidance.  

  



**Accountabilities:**  

1\. Assist investigators in obtaining scientific data by performing standardized laboratory experiments under general supervision and guidance.
  

2\. Observe, detail, record, and maintain accurate records of experimental protocols, conditions, and results.
  

3\. Apply established research methodology to ensure all research material is handled in accordance with established protocols, policies and procedures.
  

4\. Conduct literature searches to support the research project.
  

5\. Seek guidance and direction from Research Staff or Manager.
  

6\. Electrical and mechanical component diagnostic and repair
  

7\. Assist with daily/planned maintenance for various facility equipment


**Qualifications:**  

Education: Completed or currently enrolled in a relevant post\-secondary program.
  

Experience: Prior exposure to a laboratory environment.  

  



**Assets:**  

* Experience with Pneumatic automation system
* Experience with PLC programming
**Nuclear Operations Security Provisions**  

Security clearances and background checks are necessary due to the sensitive nature of the nuclear facility’s operations and regulatory licensing (Nuclear Safety Control Act) requirements. As a condition of employment for this Appointment, you must successfully complete the appropriate and necessary security screenings / clearances (documentation will follow in a separate email). You will be advised in writing by the University whether this condition has been met upon the University's receipt of the results. If you are unsuccessful in these processes, you will not be able to meet the job requirements and therefore any offer of employment will be rescinded or will result in your employment with the University will be terminated.  

  



**Being a Nuclear Energy Worker**  

You will be declared a Nuclear Energy Worker. Given the nature of the work environment where you will be performing your duties, which includes entering and working in radiological hazardous environments, the University requires the use of protective equipment such as respirators, protective clothing, and gloves, as necessary to enter these areas. The University is committed to fostering a safe and healthy work environment

The Faculty of ​Art​ invites applications for the following anticipated course offering in the Fall/Winter 2026-27 academic year:
EXAN-3009: Animated Documentary (​0.5​ credit)
(Fall 2026 Semester: September 9, 2026 – December 23, 2026; Thursday: 3:10PM - 6:10PM; Blended Delivery)
COURSE DESCRIPTION:
Framed by critical discourse on documentary media, as well as historical and contemporary examples, this course explores animation as a potent tool for elaborating non-fiction projects. Drawing on documentation, students will learn to use animation to deliver engaged commentary on issues of social and political relevance or translate personal narratives through animated media. Students will also explore the shifting notions of truth and ethical dilemmas inherent to documentary film-making and essayist videos. Through a blend of theory and practice, this course will deepen students' understanding of the unique power of animation in conveying complex non-fiction narratives.

Experience providing clear direction, mentorship and supervision to Teaching Assistants.

Job Description: **Rumble** is *the* Freedom\-First technology platform. We proudly offer a video platform, cloud services, advertising solutions, and a non\-custodial cryptocurrency wallet.


Rumble is seeking a Brand Designer to create bold, high\-impact visual work across our brand, marketing, creator, and business initiatives. This role is ideal for a designer who can translate ideas into clear, compelling creative across a wide range of formats, from landing pages and social assets to presentations, event materials, and campaign collateral. You'll help shape how Rumble shows up to creators, users, advertisers, and partners across a fast\-growing video platform built around independent voices and audience connection.



In this role, you'll bring Rumble's suite of brands to life through thoughtful, high\-quality design that is both consistent and adaptable. You should be comfortable owning work from concept to final delivery, creating reusable assets, and developing visuals that support marketing, storytelling, and business growth. Success in this role requires strong creative instincts, attention to detail, and the ability to move quickly under tight deadlines without losing sight of brand standards or strategic intent.



You'll work closely with cross\-functional partners while also collaborating with external creatives, including artists, photographers, and agencies, when needed. This role does not have a dedicated project manager, so the right candidate must be highly self\-directed, organized, and accountable for driving their own work forward. The ideal candidate is energized by a fast\-moving environment where priorities can shift and where strong design plays an important role in how the company communicates with multiple audiences.


**Responsibilities**
--------------------



Lead brand and marketing design work across a broad mix of channels, campaigns, and business needs. Create high\-quality illustrations, graphics, and other visual assets from concept through final delivery. Build and maintain reusable creative assets such as landing pages, display ads, social media content, marketing decks, presentations, event materials, and other branded collateral. Manage multiple projects independently, prioritize effectively, and deliver high\-quality work under tight timelines without day\-to\-day project management support. Partner with cross\-functional teams to develop visuals that connect with creators, Rumble users, advertisers, and business audiences. Help enforce consistency across the organization by applying and championing brand guidelines. Coordinate with external creative partners when additional support or specialized assets are needed. Contribute to other creative and brand initiatives as priorities evolve.


**Qualifications**
------------------


* 3\+ years of professional design experience, with a portfolio that demonstrates strong brand and marketing work across multiple channels and asset types.
* 3\+ years of experience designing email creative, ideally in Figma or a comparable design environment.
* Experience producing digital, presentation, and large\-format creative assets.
* Strong understanding of how to connect brand or marketing strategy to effective visual design.
* Proficiency in Figma and strong command of design fundamentals including layout, typography, hierarchy, and composition.
* Comfort working in a fast\-paced environment with changing priorities, tight deadlines, and multiple concurrent projects.
* Highly self\-directed, proactive, and organized, with the ability to manage work independently and own outcomes in an environment without dedicated project management support.
* General understanding of performance and growth marketing, and how creative work supports campaign outcomes.
* Strong collaboration and communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with cross\-functional teams and outside creative partners.
* Comfort working in Google Workspace and Microsoft Office products, especially for presentation, document, and collaborative asset development.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------


* Experience designing for technology, media, creator\-focused, or advertising\-related businesses.
* Experience creating social assets for platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube.
* Agency background or experience supporting multiple brands, campaigns, or audiences in parallel.
* Bachelor's degree in Design, Creative, Visual Communication, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience creating work that supports creator programs, audience growth, advertising, or brand partnerships.


**Annual Compensation Range:**



$100,000 \- $120,000 USD base \+ benefits \+ equity (If based in the United States)



Note: The salary range listed for this position is a good faith estimate based on experience, qualifications, and internal compensation structure. The actual salary offered varies depending on the candidate's skill level and experience. This posting refers to an active vacancy within the organization.

**Why Our Team Loves Working Here:**


* We are making a significant financial impact for our video creator community; we're proud of their success stories
* We enjoy challenging the status quo and going head\-to\-head against Big Tech
* We aren't afraid to try new things; we act fast and want to win
* We pay competitive salaries and provide great benefits


**EEO Statement:**  

Rumble is an equal opportunity employer. We promote an equal playing field where everyone has the same opportunities regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability status, or any other applicable characteristics protected by law. Rumble is an active participant in the e\-verify program.


**Physical demands of the position:**  

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for prolonged periods of time while using a computer and/or keyboard. The employee is required to communicate verbally and hear. The employee may be required to walk, reach with hands and arms, balance, and stoop or kneel. The employee may occasionally be required to lift and/or move up to 15 pounds.
